title: Postmortem: embeddings/rerank capacity drop due to KV-cache churn + model output regression
creator: Ava Kim
description: Summary of an operational incident where embedding + rerank endpoints experienced sustained capacity degradation and quality regressions. Impacted hosted customers during peak hours; root cause traced to a model variant that increased average tokenization length and a concurrent KV cache churn introduced by a configuration change, which together reduced batching efficiency and caused autoscaler thrash.
incident_summary: On 2025-11-04 we observed a ~45% throughput drop and elevated latency for embedding and rerank endpoints. Several customers reported timeouts and degraded relevance scores. The immediate user-facing cause was capacity exhaustion on the dedicated embedding pool during a high-traffic window; deeper investigation found a recent model variant rollout that expanded output sequences and a config change that reduced KV cache TTL, causing cache misses and heavier per-request work.
timeline: 2025-11-04 01:42 UTC - First automated latency alert (p50 embedding latency > 300ms) from Grafana for pool-emb-dedicated-3.
2025-11-04 01:47 UTC - Ops on-call (Diego) acknowledged; initial mitigations attempted: increase worker count in pool to handle burst.
2025-11-04 01:55 UTC - Error budgets for rerank endpoints start burning; customers A and B report 504s via support channel.
2025-11-04 02:10 UTC - Noted elevated KV cache miss rate (cache hit dropped from 93% -> 28%) and a 60% increase in average tokens per request across embedding models.
2025-11-04 02:25 UTC - Rolled back the model variant flagged in the Canary rollout (model-rerank-v2025-11-01beta) to previous stable model (model-rerank-v2025-10-28).
2025-11-04 02:40 UTC - Applied temporary config rollback: restored KV cache TTL from 30s to 10m to reduce churn.
2025-11-04 03:05 UTC - Autoscaler stabilized, throughput recovered to ~92% of baseline; latency returned near normal within 40 minutes of rollback.
2025-11-04 05:00 UTC - Incident declared resolved for customers with mitigating controls in place; follow-up postmortem opened.
2025-11-05 09:00 UTC - Engineering postmortem review with PM, Design, and SRE teams; action items assigned.
2025-11-10 16:00 UTC - Final fixes merged to main branch and scheduled for runtime-1.24 canary on 2025-11-12.
root_cause: Two independent changes converged: (1) a model variant introduced a regression that significantly expanded generated token sequences for the rerank model, increasing average sequence length and per-request compute; (2) a configuration change in KV cache TTL (shortened from 10 minutes to 30 seconds) made our prefix/KV caching ineffective under the new token distribution. The combination reduced effective batching and increased per-request GPU time, which triggered autoscaler oscillation and capacity exhaustion for the Dedicated embedding pool.
detection_and_alerting: Primary detection via Grafana latency and error-rate alerts. There was no direct alert on cache-miss rate or sudden average sequence-length change; those signals were surfaced during manual investigation. Post-incident we added a synthetic check that tracks tokens-per-request and cache-hit rate for embedding/rerank pools.
immediate_mitigations: Rolled back the canaryed rerank model to stable version (model-rerank-v2025-10-28).
Restored KV cache TTL to 10 minutes to regain prefix/KV reuse.
Temporarily increased dedicated pool worker count and set a higher max concurrency cap to absorb burst while stabilizing autoscaler settings.
Opened priority support notifications to impacted customers and issued ETA for full resolution.
Enabled conservative rate-limiting for bulk rerank endpoints for non-enterprise tiers for 90 minutes during recovery window.
Added a temporary fallback routing rule: route heavy long-sequence requests to a lower-cost, higher-latency cluster to avoid saturating critical pools.
Created a runbook checkpoint to prevent simultaneous model and infra config rollouts to the same pool in future.
Patched a monitoring dashboard to surface tokens-per-request and cache-hit trends.
Launched a second Canary with increased telemetry on 2025-11-05 to validate fixes.
Updated incident Slack channel with hourly updates until recovery.
long_term_action_items: Enforce a gating rule in rollout tooling that prevents model variant rollouts when KV cache TTL < 5 minutes for embedding/rerank pools (owner: SRE - Priya Shah, ETA: 2025-12-01).
Implement a tokens-per-request anomaly alert (owner: Observability - Mateo Alvarez, ETA: 2025-11-22).
Revise autoscaler hysteresis and add cooldown windows for Dedicated embedding pools to avoid thrash during simultaneous config changes (owner: Runtime - Diego Morales, ETA: 2025-11-30).
Add a structured pre-rollout checklist requiring performance simulations for changes that affect sequence length distribution (owner: ML Onboarding - Linh Tran, ETA: 2025-12-08).
Improve canary telemetry to include cache-hit metrics and end-to-end latency percentiles per model variant (owner: Runtime - Diego Morales, ETA: 2025-11-18).
Create an SLI for embedding quality/regression detection tied to a small held-out rerank testset to detect quality regressions automatically (owner: Research - Nora Patel, ETA: 2025-12-15).
Run a chaos test that simulates KV cache TTL reduction and a synthetic long-sequence workload to validate autoscaler behavior (owner: SRE - Priya Shah, ETA: 2025-12-20).
followups: PR #1842: add tokens-per-request and cache-hit instrumentation to ingestion proxy (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1842)
PR #1851: autoscaler cooldown and hysteresis improvements (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1851)
Customer incident notes: Zendesk ticket aggregation (ref: ZD-9302) and support playbook update.
Runbook update: embeddings runbook section 'cache and sequence length anomalies' (internal runbook link added).
Schedule a cross-team retro on 2025-11-17 with PM, Research, Runtime, and SRE to refine rollout coordination.
Add this incident to postmortem index and quarterly reliability review (Q4 reliability report).
retrospective_notes: Main takeaways: avoid coupling model rollouts with cache/infra config changes; surface tokens-per-request as a first-class telemetry signal; conservative autoscaler hysteresis for Dedicated pools is necessary to tolerate short-lived churn. Communication between ML, Runtime, and SRE teams during canaries needs to be standardized with explicit rollback criteria. We will track progress on action items in the Embedding & Rerank Stability project board.
